packet.explanation: Testing discipline means that passing one test doesn't prove a program works for all cases—you must also test edge cases, invalid inputs, and general properties to ensure true correctness.
packet.strategy: Testing discipline involves systematically checking a program's correctness beyond a single passing example. It includes testing boundary cases (like minimum/maximum values), negative tests (invalid inputs), and verifying general properties (like input-output relationships). This ensures the code behaves correctly under all expected and edge scenarios.
